text: I'll start with the deployment and the crashing pod.

remediation.name: checkout-worker
remediation.current_value: absent (no env or envFrom on the worker container; pod shows "Environment:    <none>")
remediation.required_value:
env entry AMQP_URL set to the checkout queue URL, e.g. - name: AMQP_URL
  value: amqp://rabbitmq.payments.svc.cluster.local:5672/ (or a valueFrom reference to a ConfigMap/Secret key that exists in namespace payments)

arguments.root_cause_statement: The checkout-worker Deployment's pod template starts the worker container with a shell command that refuses to run unless the environment variable AMQP_URL is set, but the template defines no env and no envFrom for that container. Every replica therefore starts, finds AMQP_URL empty, prints "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set" and exits 1, so the kubelet holds the pod in CrashLoopBackOff and the Deployment never reports a ready replica. Because no pod ever reaches the consume loop, checkout jobs are never pulled from the queue. There is also no ConfigMap or Secret in the payments namespace carrying that value, so the fix is to add the AMQP_URL environment variable (or a source object plus a reference to it) to the Deployment's pod template.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment payments/checkout-worker declares no .spec.template.spec.containers[worker].env (and no envFrom), while that container's command requires AMQP_URL to be non-empty; with AMQP_URL unset the container prints "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set" and exits with code 1 on every start, leaving the container in CrashLoopBackOff.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment has no ready replicas and its only pod is crash-looping.
The worker container is in CrashLoopBackOff after repeatedly exiting with Error.
The Deployment pod template's worker container requires AMQP_URL but declares no env or envFrom.
evidence.quote: [ -n \"${AMQP_URL:-}\" ] || { echo \"FATAL: AMQP_URL not set\"; exit 1; }; echo \"connected to queue at ${AMQP_URL}\"; while :; do echo \"consuming checkout jobs\"; sleep 10; done

evidence.claim: The running container has no environment variables at all.
The container's own log states the exact reason it exits: AMQP_URL is unset.
The container terminated with exit code 1, matching the guard clause in the command.
No Secret exists in the payments namespace that could supply the value, so the value must be added to the Deployment (or a new source object created).
evidence.quote: 0 objects of kind secrets in namespace payments

ruled_out.alternative: A ConfigMap key reference in the pod template broke (renamed or deleted key), which would make the pod fail with CreateContainerConfigError
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The only ConfigMap in the namespace is the cluster CA bundle with key ca.crt, and the pod template makes no configMapKeyRef/envFrom reference at all — env is simply absent, so nothing was unresolved; the container did start.

ruled_out.alternative: Image pull failure or scheduling/capacity problem keeping the pod from running
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod was scheduled and the image was already present and started six times; the failure happens after the container starts, not before.
ruled_out.quote: Normal   Pulled     84s (x6 over 4m27s)  kubelet            spec.containers{worker}: Container image "busybox:1.36" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod

ruled_out.alternative: Service account / RBAC identity problem preventing the worker from doing its job
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod runs as the default service account and mounts its token normally; it dies in its own entrypoint guard before making any API or queue call.

ruled_out.alternative: A failing readiness probe or Service selector mismatch hiding a healthy pod
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod template defines no probes and no Service exists in the namespace; the container itself terminates with Error.
